yarn-troppo.meaning: All the beats survive, but it reframes the piece as past ("Back in the day, the trickiest bit of a weekend away was getting out of bed.") and invents details: "the pipes'd start banging", "looking like they're up to no good", "hanging onto a mandolin for dear life".
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms mostly fit: "have a squiz", "scruffier-looking mob", "dodgy-looking barges", "Ripper, even" for bully. "That's when it all goes pear-shaped" anticipates a disaster rather than a misunderstanding waiting to happen.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Much is natural ("plonk yourself on the edge of the bed", "nothing for it but"), but stock interjections are bolted on: "Fair dinkum.", "Strewth.", "head cocked like a kelpie hearing the ute".
yarn-troppo.register: Well past level 2: a pub-yarn layer of tags and similes, "Fair dinkum", "Strewth", "'em", "ya", "careful as a cat burglar"; no swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The comedy survives but is broadened; the original's dry, mock-solemn understatement becomes knockabout: "waving her arm about like she's giving you the whole joint".
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively and mostly smooth, though the opening stacks interjections: "Fair dinkum. Now, if it's a big house-party, easy, cos".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisable, but the added similes and the past-tense framing smother the original's deadpan, second-person shape.

engine.meaning: The original, nearly unchanged; every point survives.
engine.sense: Of three swaps, one takes the wrong place: "To my beaut friends the Elbridges" puts slang into a 1907 inscription the narrator is quoting. "At what time is brekkie?" pairs slang with stiff syntax.
engine.authenticity: The few swaps sit oddly in untouched Edwardian prose: "At what time is brekkie?"
engine.register: Essentially untranslated: "brekkie", "beaut", "righto" in otherwise original text; far under level 2.
engine.tone: The original's tone is intact, as the text is.
engine.flow: Reads as the original, bar the jarring "At what time is brekkie?"

unharnessed.meaning: Every point survives, the bath, pictures, books and the Emerson joke included: "So they reckoned that'd be over your head, did they?"
unharnessed.sense: Every term fits: "perfectly bonzer" matches the dated 'bully', "Pretty scruffy-looking mob", "dodgy-looking barges", "almost on the sly".
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian telling it: "Sleep in as long as you like", "the only thing for it is to get dressed and go out for a wander round the grounds".
unharnessed.register: A light, even Aussie layer, right for level 2: "bonzer", "mob", "righto", "reckoned"; no swearing.
unharnessed.tone: The dry, wry, second-person comedy is whole: "Some people _are_ like that."
unharnessed.flow: Smooth throughout: "Scratch the bath as too noisy. And so, very carefully, almost on the sly, you set about getting dressed."

yarn-deadset.meaning: Every point survives, close to the original's structure.
yarn-deadset.sense: Mostly exact ("have a squiz out", "scruffy-looking mob", "dodgy-looking barges"), but "perfectly ripper" strains: ripper doesn't take 'perfectly' easily.
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Mostly natural, with some stiff carry-overs: "You suppose they reckoned that'd be over your head, did they?", "Maybe open it modestly and have a squiz out".
yarn-deadset.register: A light layer at about level 2: "cos", "brekkie", "squiz", "uni", "righto".
yarn-deadset.tone: Keeps the wry deadpan: "Some people _are_ like that."
yarn-deadset.flow: Readable, with some clunky joins where slang meets the original's syntax: "Opening, at the red ribbon:" and "You suppose they reckoned".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point survives; "Takes you about two seconds" renders the work of a moment.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "no worries" for the simple problem, "have a squiz out", "Pretty scruffy-looking mob", "that vague it's downright terrifying". "It's a lovely thought, and all" loses a little of bully's slang flavour but keeps the sense.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural throughout: "it's that vague it's downright terrifying", "Fair enough, I s'pose", "nothing for it but to get dressed".
yarn-dinkum.register: A light-to-moderate layer, right for level 2: "no worries", "brekkie", "squiz", "mob", "'em".
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the wry, self-mocking deadpan: "Well, we'll show 'em! We'll read it just out of spite."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Back over onto the cool pillow till twenty past. Then up on your elbow again".

yarn-troppo.quote: Back in the day, the trickiest bit of a weekend away was getting out of bed.
yarn-troppo.original: Take, for example, the matter of arising in the morning.
yarn-troppo.why: Reframes a present-tense 'for example' as a reminiscence; it is not the original's opening move.
Stock interjection bolted on; with 'Strewth.' it reads as stage-Australian.

yarn-troppo.quote: And you know if you turned on the bath, the pipes'd start banging and you'd wake the whole house.
yarn-troppo.original: Probably, if you started your tub, you'd wake the whole house.

yarn-troppo.quote: head cocked like a kelpie hearing the ute
yarn-troppo.original: with head cocked on one side
yarn-troppo.why: Bush simile added; heavier than the brief asks.

yarn-troppo.quote: That's when it all goes pear-shaped, a frightful misunderstanding just waiting to happen.
yarn-troppo.original: there is apt to be a frightful misunderstanding
yarn-troppo.why: 'goes pear-shaped' says it has already gone wrong, then the line hedges; a clunky double rendering.

engine.quote: To my beaut friends the Elbridges
engine.original: To my good friends the Elbridges
engine.why: Changes a quoted inscription by a third party; slang in a document the narrator is reading is the wrong place.
Slang in formal syntax: a word swap, not a voice.

engine.quote: Take, for example, the matter of arising in the morning.
engine.original: Take, for example, the matter of arising in the morning.
engine.why: Left untranslated throughout; far under a level-2 brief.

unharnessed.why: Slightly loses the grudging 'at that'; harmless.

yarn-deadset.quote: The feeling behind this is perfectly ripper
yarn-deadset.original: The sentiment in this attitude is perfectly bully

yarn-deadset.quote: You suppose they reckoned that'd be over your head, did they?
yarn-deadset.original: You suppose they thought that would be over your head, did they?
yarn-deadset.why: 'You suppose they reckoned' stacks two verbs of thinking: clunky.

yarn-deadset.quote: Maybe open it modestly and have a squiz out.
yarn-deadset.original: Perhaps open it modestly and peer out.

yarn-dinkum.quote: Hello, there's some books on the table.
yarn-dinkum.original: Hello, here are some books on the table.
yarn-dinkum.why: 'there's some books' is colloquial and fine aloud, but reads a touch sloppy on the page.
A slightly weaker rendering of the original's comic 'clandestinely'.

summaries.yarn-troppo: Energetic and varied, but over-cooked for level 2, with stock interjections and invented detail that swamp the deadpan.
summaries.engine: The original with three word swaps, one of which wrongly alters a quoted inscription.
summaries.unharnessed: A light, natural, faithful retelling at the right weight; the best of the set with E.
summaries.yarn-deadset: A faithful light retelling at the right weight; a little more literal and clunky than C or E.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: A natural, varied, faithful light retelling; with C the best.
